newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's food self-sufficiency rate falls.
newsitem.headline: Japan's food self-sufficiency rate falls.

text.p: Japan's food self-sufficiency rate fell to 42 percent in the fiscal year ended March 1996, a report released by the Agriculture Ministry said on Friday. The rate, which is domestic production as a percentage of total food demand, compared with 73 percent in fiscal 1965.
The decline was mainly due to a fall in domestic food production and changes in the Japanese diet, it said.
It said an increasing trend for Japanese to eat less rice but more meat and dairy products had also helped lower the nation's self-sufficiency rate in grain.

"As for food production, the total cultivated area declined by 39 percent between calendar year 1960 and 1995, due to declines in both the arable land area and the percentage of arable land utilised," the report said.
The report said Japan needed to expand domestic food production in order to halt the fall in its food self-sufficiency rate, especially amid expected rapid growth in the global population.

An expansion of world grain production had outpaced population growth in China, India, the United States and Indonesia, which together account for about half the world's six billion people, the report said.
